items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The type names (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookie and so on) say what they are, and every public field has a doc comment that states its dedup and ordering rules. The new consistent_hash.go follows the existing plugin file layout, and the code passes make analyze.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The logic lives in its own consistent_hash.go. The IR is built once in the constructor, the apply step only sets RouteAction.HashPolicy, and the merge is a separate function. Dedup and canonical ordering are shared helpers used by both build and merge. Generated code came from make go-generate-apis.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: CEL rule enforces disable exclusivity. kubebuilder markers set MinLength, MaxLength and MaxItems, plus a TTL pattern. An invalid ttl is reported as an error on the policy rather than dropped. Nil checks are in place ('if ch == nil || action == nil'). The MaxItems=16 cap is a deliberate API limit.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: The golden output shows the union with the higher-priority policy first, deduped, back in canonical order (headers x-a, x-shared, x-b, then cookie cb, then query qa). sourceIp comes from the higher-priority policy only. Metadata records 'consistentHash' under merge.TrafficPolicy.gateway.kgateway.dev listing both policies.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: An empty {} defaults to a single sourceIp hash policy. A rule-level disable clears inherited hash_policy, which the disable-route golden test covers. The CEL rule '!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (...)' rejects disable combined with other fields and appears in the generated CRD YAML.
